previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and recurrent tracheitis was admitted due to worsening cough, increased green sputum, and severe throat and chest pain despite being on outpatient ciprofloxacin and doxycycline. She had intermittent chills but no fever or respiratory distress. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and sputum cultures were repeatedly contaminated. She was treated with IV vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin based on prior MRSA and Pseudomonas infections. Her pain improved with continued use of gabapentin, oxycodone, and acetaminophen/ibuprofen. She gradually resumed oral intake and was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of IV vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin, with follow-up arranged with pulmonology, ENT, interventional pulmonology, and infectious disease.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with a history of 
tracheobronchomalacia s/p tracheostomy at age ___, s/p multiple 
airway reconstructions, with recurrent bronchotracheitis, s/p 
recent tracheostomy revision, cricoid split and ___ placement 
on ___ with multiple recent admissions for tracheitis, 
presenting with productive cough, shortness of breath and 
neck/chest pain.

#  Increased sputum production/cough
The patient presented with reported increased sputum production 
and cough, despite being startd on levofloxacin as an outpatient 
two days prior as an outpatient. She received a 1 x dose of 1g 
Vancomycin/2 gm Cefepime in the ED due to concern for bacterial 
tracheitis given the patient's history of recurrent tracheitis 
and previous endotracheal sputum cultures growing pseudomonas. 
However the patient remained afebrile, hemodynamically stable 
and without leukocytosis throughout her stay. ENT was consulted, 
and the patient underwent a fiberoptic exam which was notable 
for crusting around the proximal arm of the ___, but 
otherwise the t tube was noted to be in good position, and there 
were no noted physical exam findings to suggest the etiology of 
the patients pain. She was continued on humidified trach mask at 
night and saline irrigations during the day. During her stay 
there was no evidence of large volume/green secretions. Though 
an endotracheal sputum culture returned with 4+ GPC/sparse 
growth of coag + staph and gram negative rods (which resulted to 
be MRSA and Pseudomonas as on previous admission), this was 
thought most likely due to colonization vs. acute infection. 
Blood culture remained without growth. Given the above findings, 
further antibiotics were held given low concern for bacterial 
infection. She was started on a course of inhaled budesonide to 
be continued as an outpatient as a trial to decrease airway 
inflammation. There was some concern that patient anxiety was 
playing a role in her frequent suctioning, and that she was 
causing trauma/irritation. Her outpatient providers (PCP, ___, 
ENT, IP, Pulm) were contacted in an attempt to address the 
patients presentation and multiple recent admissions. They were 
in agreement with the plan to hold antibiotics and have close 
outpatient follow, and she will follow up with her PCP, ___, ENT, 
and pulmonology.  

# Dysphagia
On admission the patient endorsed dysphagia as well as some 
odynophagia to solids. The patient underwent a double contrast 
upper GI series during the admission which was notable for 
minimal narrowing of the upper esophagus near the level of the 
tracheostomy, but without any obstruction or holdup of ingested 
contrast. She was tolerating a regular diet well throughout 
admission. 

#  Chronic Pain
The patient endorse chest and throat pain on admission, similar 
to the pain she has had on previous admissions. She was 
initially treated in the ED with multiple doses of IV dilaudid, 
which was tapered on the floor. Her PO oxycodone was increased 
from 5 mg to 7.5 mg BID. She was otherwise continued on her home 
regimen of gabapentin, Tylenol and ibuprofen. The patients pain 
was well controlled with the above oral regimen on discharge. 
Outpatient follow up with the pain clinic is being arranged. The 
patient will have close follow up with her PCP ___ 
has been following her chronic pain. 

CHRONIC ISSUES
==================
# Dizziness
Patient was noted to be dizzy on admission that improved with 
boluses of IVF. This was thought possibly hypovolemic in the 
setting of her neck pain as above, but was tolerating PO 
thoughout the admission.

# Depression
The patient continued home fluoxetine.

# GERD
The patient continued home omeprazole and ranitidine. 

# Chronic microcytic anemia
The patient was noted to have  a stable microcytic anemia near 
her baseline around ___. Iron studies were resent and notable 
for a ferritin of 12 and iron of 30. There were no signs of 
active bleeding during the admission and no blood transfusions 
were required. This will need further evaluation as an 
outpatient. 

Transitional Issues
=====================
- PCP follow up of iron studies as an outpatient
- Consider sending TSH given low ferritin level, normal iron
- PCP to coordinate counseling for patient as an outpatient due 
to concern for patient anxiety as contributing factor regarding 
concern for secretions/chronic neck pain
- Per pharmacy, recommend continuing home ranitidne QHS due to 
concern of interaction with PPI
- Continue inhaled budesonide until next appointment with 
ENT/Pulmonology
- Oxycodone liquid slightly increased upon discharge for 7 day 
course
- F/u sputum studies at next ID/ENT/Pulm visit
